lots.guide_summary: All SOLD, all Gowans Hobart hammers (premium extra) in Sept 2026 for the same Eaglemoss cased Bond series: $4.58 to $6.92 a car. Scaled to our 24 cars that is about $110 to $165 hammer. No unsold or asking evidence kept. AUD, no conversion.
lots.working: Lowest same-item SOLD rate is Gowans 12 cars for $55 = $4.58 a car; x 24 cars = $110. keep_max = 110 / 1.22 = 90.2, rounded down to $90 (all-in $109.80). Flip: likely resale about 24 x $5.50 = $132 hammer at Gowans; less about 17.6% seller commission and fees (assumed, about $23) and $0 postage (local drop-off) = about $109 net; 109 / 2.44 = 44.7, rounded down to $40. Flip margin is thin, so KEEP only.
lots.confidence_reason: Film-title plinths readable in the photos (for example Ford Thunderbird Thunderball, Austin Mini On Her Majesty's Secret Service), and four recent Tasmanian SOLD results for the same series whose API records I opened and whose photos I viewed. The only uncertainty is the exact count and per-car scaling.
lots.dropped_entries: Dropped eBay.de/eBay UK asking range GBP 6.99 to 85.50 (snippet only, eBay returns 403, single new-in-box issues, not comparable to a bulk lot). Dropped Wikipedia GBP 7.99 cover price (retail new price, not market evidence). Corrected the researcher's count from about 40 to about 24 cars (photos 2 and 3 show 24). Added Gowans lots 437529 and 440665, which the researcher missed.
lots.key_photo_findings: Photos 2 and 3 show 24 cased models, each with a printed plinth naming car and film, in the standard Eaglemoss perspex case. Photo 1 shows them packed in two cardboard trays, roughly 20 visible. No magazines, no outer boxes. Mostly the less sought-after support vehicles, no Aston Martins or Lotus seen.
lots.condition: Cases look intact and clear in the photos; some cases look dusty. Cannot see whether any models are loose or missing mirrors and aerials.
lots.question_for_armitage: How many cased cars are in the lot (photos suggest 24), and are any cases cracked or models loose inside?
